cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put this envelope in your coat pocket before Mum comes in. Flat, please; don't fold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall I tell her you asked me to take it home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. A handover isn't a family announcement. Just take your coat with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming in. She'll ask why I'm wearing it at the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over your arm, then. With the pocket facing you. Let me do the talking.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs a careful handover before Mum arrives. B2's proposed announcement lets A3 specify confidentiality; A5 corrects conspicuous coat use to keep B helping without learning the contents.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 can reasonably ask about telling Mum after A1's handling request. A3 says not to announce it, and B4's coat-at-table objection causes A5's carrying correction.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks clarity about what Mum should be told; B4 anticipates a conspicuous action. These are sensible helper contributions rather than staged incompetence.

heightening.evidence: A5 shifts from telling B how to store the envelope to managing how B and A will appear when B4's arrival occurs.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies envelope, pocket and Mum's impending arrival; B4 places them at a table. Carrying the coat over an arm requires no unseen action to understand.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's clipped handover distinction corrects B's proposed disclosure; A5 gives only carrying and speaking directions needed for B4's problem.
